narrative_paragraphs: The owner claims demurrage of EUR 84,375.00 arising from the discharge at Rotterdam. The charter party allowed 72.0 laytime hours on a SHINC basis. The vessel used 117.0 laytime hours, producing an overrun of 45.0 hours. At the contractual demurrage rate of EUR 1,875.00 per hour, the demurrage due is EUR 84,375.00. The claim is presented on the basis that all time between laytime commencement and completion of discharge counts unless a valid contractual exception is established.

Laytime commenced at 12:00 LT on 14 May 2026, being six hours after NOR was tendered at 06:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e2), as prescribed by CP Clause 6. The vessel had arrived at Maasvlakte anchorage at 05:00 LT that morning (e1), but the pre-NOR period generates no laytime obligation. The WIBON character of the fixture means that time ran continuously through the berthing manoeuvre (e4, all fast at 20:00 LT on 14 May 2026) and from commencement of discharge at 22:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e5) through to completion of discharge at 09:00 LT on 19 May 2026 (e8). No exception is in contention for any of those periods.

The sole contested window runs from 12:00 LT to 16:00 LT on 17 May 2026 (e6 to e7), a period of 4.0 hours. The charterer claims this time is excluded under CP Clause 14 on the ground that rain interrupted discharge. CP Clause 14 is an express exception with a quantified threshold: precipitation must exceed 0.5 mm per hour for the period claimed, and the burden of demonstrating that the threshold is met rests explicitly with the charterer. No meteorological data, port authority precipitation record, or independent weather station report has been produced in the SoF or in any supporting document to substantiate the claim. Absent such evidence, the exception cannot be activated and the 4.0 hours count in full as laytime consumed. The incremental demurrage at risk in this window is EUR 7,500.00 (4.0 hours × EUR 1,875.00 per hour).

If the charterer produces precipitation records that satisfy the CP Clause 14 threshold for the full four-hour window, the owner's demurrage entitlement would reduce by EUR 7,500.00 to EUR 76,875.00. The owner should therefore press the charterer to disclose the specific meteorological data relied upon. Partial rainfall — for example, precipitation exceeding 0.5 mm/hr for only part of the claimed window — would reduce the excluded period proportionally. Any gap in the meteorological record defaults in favour of the owner.

The total demurrage claim of EUR 84,375.00, or EUR 76,875.00 in the event the weather exception is partially conceded, falls within the contractual time bar applicable under the charter party. The claim is supported by the SoF event sequence (e1 through e8), the SHINC laytime basis, and the NOR tender record. The owner's position on every non-contested period is unambiguous; the only genuine dispute is the four-hour weather stoppage at e6–e7, where the burden lies firmly with the charterer.

flagged_events.title: Charterer's claim of CP Clause 14 weather exception for rain stoppage 12:00–16:00 LT on 17 May 2026 is unsupported by precipitation evidence.
flagged_events.summary: The charterer contends that precipitation exceeding 0.5 mm per hour suspended laytime between e6 (rain stoppage, 12:00 LT on 17 May 2026) and e7 (discharge resumed, 16:00 LT on 17 May 2026), a period of 4.0 hours. CP Clause 14 conditions the exception on the charterer demonstrating that the threshold was met. No meteorological or port authority precipitation record has been tendered in the SoF or annexed documents. The owner's position is that the 4.0 hours count as laytime consumed and, the vessel already being on demurrage, translate directly into EUR 7,500.00 of recoverable demurrage.
flagged_events.owner_argument: CP Clause 14 places the burden of proof squarely on the charterer to demonstrate precipitation exceeding 0.5 mm per hour at the place of discharge for each hour of the claimed exception. The SoF records a rain stoppage commencing at e6 (12:00 LT, 17 May 2026) but provides no precipitation measurements. In the absence of qualifying meteorological evidence, the precondition in CP Clause 14 is not satisfied and the 4.0-hour window is treated as ordinary laytime under the SHINC basis established in the headline terms. The full 4.0 hours therefore remain on demurrage, generating EUR 7,500.00 at the contractual rate.
flagged_events.charterer_argument: The SoF records at e6 that discharge was stopped due to rain at 12:00 LT on 17 May 2026 and did not resume until e7 (16:00 LT, 17 May 2026). The charterer would argue that this contemporaneous entry constitutes prima facie evidence of a weather stoppage and that CP Clause 14 should be read as requiring only reasonable evidence of precipitation rather than instrument-grade measurement data. The charterer may also seek to rely on publicly available weather station records for Rotterdam-Maasvlakte for the period in question to establish that the 0.5 mm/hr threshold was exceeded, contending that the SoF entry corroborates those records.

packet.dispute_narrative_markdown:
## Background

MT Aegean Pioneer completed a voyage from Ras Tanura to Rotterdam under the charter party dated 12 February 2026. The charter party allowed 72.0 laytime hours on a SHINC basis. The vessel consumed 117.0 laytime hours at the discharge port, producing an overrun of 45.0 hours. At the contractual demurrage rate of EUR 45,000.00 per day pro rata, the demurrage due is EUR 84,375.00.

## Laytime Commencement and Voyage Chronology

MT Aegean Pioneer arrived at Maasvlakte anchorage at 05:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e1). NOR was tendered at 06:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e2). Pursuant to CP Clause 6, laytime commenced six hours thereafter at 12:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e3). The vessel proceeded to berth and was all fast at 20:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e4). Discharge commenced at 22:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e5). Time ran continuously through the berthing manoeuvre and throughout cargo operations. Discharge was completed at 09:00 LT on 19 May 2026 (e8). No exception is in contention for any period of the voyage outside the window addressed below.

## Disputed Weather Stoppage: 12:00–16:00 LT on 17 May 2026

The sole contested period runs from 12:00 LT to 16:00 LT on 17 May 2026 (e6 to e7), a duration of 4.0 hours. The SoF records a stoppage attributed to rain at e6 (Stoppage — rain claimed by charterer, 12:00 LT on 17 May 2026). Discharge resumed at e7 (16:00 LT on 17 May 2026). The charterer invokes CP Clause 14, which excludes time lost to precipitation only where rainfall at the place of discharge exceeds 0.5 mm per hour for the period claimed. CP Clause 14 expressly places the burden of demonstrating that threshold on the charterer.

## Owner's Position on the Weather Exception

No meteorological data, port authority precipitation record, KNMI station printout, or independent weather station report has been produced in the SoF or in any annexe to substantiate the charterer's assertion. A contemporaneous SoF entry recording a stoppage does not of itself satisfy the evidentiary burden imposed by CP Clause 14. In the absence of qualifying precipitation evidence, the precondition of CP Clause 14 is not met and the 4.0-hour window counts in full as laytime consumed. As the vessel was already on demurrage at the time of the stoppage, those 4.0 hours translate directly into EUR 7,500.00 of recoverable demurrage. Should the charterer produce precipitation records, the owner will assess them against the 0.5 mm/hr threshold on an hour-by-hour basis; any gap in the record defaults in favour of the owner.

## Time Bar

The total demurrage claim of EUR 84,375.00 is presented within the contractual time bar applicable under the charter party. The time bar date, calculated at 90 days from completion of discharge on 19 May 2026, falls on 17 August 2026. This claim is submitted with 81 days remaining before that date. All rights are reserved in respect of any revision to the claim quantum following disclosure of meteorological evidence by the charterer.
packet.claim_letter_markdown:
**Aegean Tankers S.A.**
Owners of MT Aegean Pioneer

27 May 2026

North Sea Crude Trading B.V.
Attn: Claims Department

Dear Sirs,

**Re: Demurrage Claim — MT Aegean Pioneer — Ras Tanura / Rotterdam — CP dated 12 February 2026**

We write on behalf of Aegean Tankers S.A. as owners of MT Aegean Pioneer (the "Vessel") in connection with the charter party dated 12 February 2026 (the "CP") between Aegean Tankers S.A. as owners and North Sea Crude Trading B.V. as charterers, for the carriage of cargo from Ras Tanura to Rotterdam. Following completion of discharge at Rotterdam on 19 May 2026, we hereby present our formal demurrage claim as set out below.

**1. Summary of claim**
- Laytime allowed: 72.0 hours SHINC
- Laytime used: 117.0 hours
- Time on demurrage: 45.0 hours
- Demurrage rate: EUR 45,000.00 per day pro rata
- Demurrage due: EUR 84,375.00

**2. Statement of facts**

The Vessel arrived at Maasvlakte anchorage at 05:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e1 — Arrived at Maasvlakte anchorage, 05:00 LT, 14 May 2026). Notice of Readiness was tendered at 06:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e2 — NOR tendered, 06:00 LT, 14 May 2026). Pursuant to CP Clause 6, which provides that laytime shall commence six hours after tender of NOR, berth or no berth, or upon commencement of cargo operations, whichever first occurs, laytime commenced at 12:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e3 — Laytime commenced, 12:00 LT, 14 May 2026). The six-hour notice period ran continuously from NOR tender; no event prior to 12:00 LT on 14 May 2026 reduces or interrupts laytime.

The Vessel shifted from anchorage and was all fast at berth at 20:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e4 — All fast at berth, 20:00 LT, 14 May 2026). Time ran continuously through the berthing manoeuvre in accordance with the SHINC laytime basis. Discharge commenced at 22:00 LT on 14 May 2026 (e5 — Commenced discharge, 22:00 LT, 14 May 2026).

At 12:00 LT on 17 May 2026, discharge was stopped (e6 — Stoppage — rain claimed by charterer, 12:00 LT, 17 May 2026). The charterer asserts that this stoppage is attributable to rain and claims an exclusion under CP Clause 14. Discharge resumed at 16:00 LT on 17 May 2026 (e7 — Resumed discharge, 16:00 LT, 17 May 2026). The owner's position on this period is set out in full in Section 3 below.

Discharge was completed at 09:00 LT on 19 May 2026 (e8 — Completed discharge, 09:00 LT, 19 May 2026). The total laytime consumed from commencement (e3) to completion of discharge (e8), inclusive of all disputed and undisputed periods, is 117.0 hours. Against the contractual allowance of 72.0 hours, the overrun on demurrage is 45.0 hours.

**3. Disputed time**

**3.1 Charterer's purported CP Clause 14 weather exception — rain stoppage 12:00–16:00 LT on 17 May 2026 (e6–e7): EUR 7,500.00**

The charterer contends that the 4.0-hour period between e6 (Stoppage — rain claimed by charterer, 12:00 LT, 17 May 2026) and e7 (Resumed discharge, 16:00 LT, 17 May 2026) is excluded from laytime and demurrage pursuant to CP Clause 14. That clause provides that time lost due to rain shall not count as laytime only where precipitation at the place of discharge exceeds 0.5 mm per hour for the period claimed, and expressly places the burden of demonstrating that condition on the charterer.

No meteorological data, port authority precipitation record, KNMI station printout, or independent weather station report has been produced in the Statement of Facts or in any document annexed to the charterer's communications to substantiate that the 0.5 mm/hr threshold was met during any part of the claimed window. The SoF entry at e6 records a stoppage attributed to rain as a contemporaneous operational notation; it does not constitute, and is not a substitute for, the evidentiary burden imposed by CP Clause 14. In the absence of qualifying precipitation evidence, the precondition of CP Clause 14 is not satisfied, and the exception cannot be activated. The 4.0 hours therefore count in full as laytime consumed under the SHINC basis and, the Vessel being on demurrage at the commencement of the stoppage, translate directly into recoverable demurrage of EUR 7,500.00. We call upon the charterer to produce forthwith any meteorological evidence upon which reliance is placed; absent such disclosure, the owner's position on this period is maintained in full.

**4. Time bar**

This claim is submitted within the contractual time bar of 90 days from completion of discharge, which falls on 17 August 2026.

**5. Supporting documents**

The following documents are enclosed in support of this claim and the figures set out above:

1. Charter Party dated 12 February 2026 (including all riders and addenda)
2. Notice of Readiness (NOR) — tendered 06:00 LT, 14 May 2026
3. Statement of Facts (SoF) — Rotterdam, events e1 through e8
4. Laytime calculation sheet
5. Port authority or terminal precipitation log for Maasvlakte, 17 May 2026, 12:00–16:00 LT (requested from charterer; to be provided by charterer in support of any CP Clause 14 exception)
6. Independent meteorological station printout (KNMI or equivalent) confirming hourly precipitation measurements for 17 May 2026, 12:00–16:00 LT (requested from charterer)
7. Terminal or ship's log entry recording suspension and resumption of cargo operations on 17 May 2026

**6. Demand**

We accordingly demand payment of EUR 84,375.00 within 30 days of the date of this letter to our nominated bank account, details of which have been previously notified to you under separate cover.

All rights reserved.

Yours faithfully,

For and on behalf of
**Aegean Tankers S.A.**
Owners of MT Aegean Pioneer
